summary.note: Star/fork/last-push/license figures observed Nov 24, 2026 via GitHub repo pages or search results dated then. 'not captured' means the figure was not shown in the page read, not that it does not exist.

repos.claim: Autonomous hedge fund: 4 AI agents trading live on Solana; replaces a quant trading desk.
repos.last_push: not captured (37 commits total; created 2024-12-10; 0 releases)
repos.reason: Real repo, but live-money Solana trading bot with only 37 commits and no releases; 'autonomous hedge fund' is unvalidated. Excluded for live trading per standing rule.

repos.claim: DAG-driven trading floor: 77 finance skills, 29 agent swarms debating trades in real time; replaces a pro terminal + analyst.
repos.last_push: active Nov 24, 2026 (news updated that day; 3,996 commits, 16 releases)
repos.reason: Real, actively maintained HKU project (arXiv 2611.24845). Can live-trade with user-set limits; no verified returns; heavy and complex. Research only, never live.

repos.claim: Bloomberg Terminal on your laptop: CFA-level analytics, 100+ data connectors, 37 AI investor agents; replaces Bloomberg (~$27,000/yr).
repos.reason: Real and popular, but 'Bloomberg replacement' is overstated: no real-time exchange data included, data/LLM bills are yours, Enterprise is $15-$45/user/mo.

repos.claim: Every model ChatGPT runs plus Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek + 20 more, self-hosted, native MCP, your keys; replaces ChatGPT Plus.
repos.reason: Claim essentially true. Real, huge, actively maintained. Needs own API keys + self-hosting, which is the honest cost.

repos.claim: 200+ AI models behind one self-hosted dashboard; replaces juggling Midjourney + Runway + Sora subs.
repos.reason: Real repo; current README says 800+ models (Reel's 200+ is stale-low). It is a control panel, not GPUs: generation runs through paid MuAPI, and it markets 'Uncensored / NSFW AI'. Not free to actually generate.

repos.claim: Offline Live2D AI companion that sees your screen, hears your voice, shows its inner thoughts before it speaks; replaces AI companion apps.
repos.license: NOASSERTION (unclear; Live2D sample models under separate license)
repos.reason: Claim mostly true and repo is real, but it is a niche VTuber companion with low utility for Ankit; v2.0 rewrite in planning and long-term memory temporarily removed.

repos.claim: Free Claude Code skill: 209 verified checks across 6 ad platforms, 6 subagents in parallel, one Ads Health Score; replaces an agency ad audit.
repos.last_push: not captured (149 commits, 18 releases; created 2026-02-11; 12 platforms)
repos.reason: Repo is real, but the Reel's core claim is false: the README's own 'Project status' section says it is a 'development candidate... not release-ready' and 'All twelve account-health scoring profiles are disabled, so no health score is produced.' The Ads Health Score does not currently exist.

repos.claim: Cloudflare's open-source AI email client on Workers; each mailbox in its own Durable Object; your email never leaves your account; replaces Superhuman / AI inbox.
repos.reason: Real Cloudflare example app and the Durable-Object/draft-confirmation claims check out, but the README warns any user passing the shared Cloudflare Access policy can access ALL mailboxes by design (no per-mailbox auth), and it needs your own domain + Cloudflare account. Thin history (11 commits).

repos.claim: Makes an agent's browser invisible to bot detection (Camoufox C++-level spoofing); accessibility tree cuts token cost ~90%; replaces commercial stealth-scraping APIs.
repos.reason: Repo is real and the ~90% token-cut claim matches the README. But its core purpose is bypassing bot detection/Cloudflare, which is a ToS risk on target sites, and it sends opt-out crash telemetry to GitHub Issues.

repos.claim: HeyGen's open-source video framework: agent writes plain HTML, it renders an MP4. No React, no JSX; replaces paid programmatic-video SaaS.
repos.reason: Claim true. Real HeyGen project, very actively maintained. Studio app has a free plan; Pro is $25/mo for top models.

repos.claim: 1 Claude = 13 agents (ig-reel, ig-viral, ig-caption...), 26 hook formulas, virality research, content calendar; approval before posting.
repos.reason: Real repo; 13 skills and 26 hook formulas check out, and it is directly relevant to KRCA social work. But only 2 commits, and the author's own tests show the hook scorer is AUC 0.56 at picking winners (coin flip) - it kills weak hooks only.

repos.claim: OmniRoute setup commands PDF (OmniRoute_Claude_Code_Commands.pdf) linked from the OmniRoute how-to Reel.
repos.last_push: not captured (15 commits; no license shown)
repos.reason: Real but trivial: a small collection of PDFs. Only notable as the source of the OmniRoute setup commands; the OmniRoute verdict itself is UNCERTAIN.

repos.claim: Open-source GitHub project with over 220K stars; a single instruction file (CLAUDE.md) with 4 rules: think before coding, keep it simple, change only what is needed, verify the code works.
repos.last_push: not captured (28 commits; created 2026-01-27; single CLAUDE.md)
repos.reason: Star claim true (235k). NOT by Karpathy - by multica-ai, distilled from his public observations (already adopted as Ankit's karpathy-coding-rules skill). Note: README install instructions reference a different owner marketplace (forrestchang/andrej-karpathy-skills).

repos.claim: Free AI trading team: 4 analysts (fundamentals, news, sentiment, technical), bull vs bear debate, trader -> risk team -> portfolio manager chain, decision log vs actual returns; works with US and Indian tickers, Ollama or LLM key.
repos.reason: Real, huge, research-only (README: 'does not place trades'). But the Reel describes the original 2024 LangGraph framework; the current repo is a rebuilt terminal agent needing a Tauric API key (or other LLM key) for data. The bull/bear debate structure is no longer in the current README.

repos.claim: Agents that run real browser workflows (from the '7 repos to build AI agents' list).
repos.last_push: v1.0.8, very active (11,073 commits, 157 releases; created 2024-10-31)
repos.reason: Real, huge, actively maintained. Rebuilt around CDP/REPL. Cloud browsers are $0.06/browser-hour; local use needs your own model API key.

repos.claim: Free GitHub repo giving 800M+ (Reel 1) / 1.5B (Reel 3) free AI tokens/month by routing across providers' free tiers (Google, Groq, Mistral, NVIDIA, Cerebras, Cloudflare...).
repos.last_push: active Nov 24, 2026 (15,572 commits, 284 releases; default branch release/v3.8.55; created 2026-02-13)
repos.reason: Repo is real and huge, and its README now claims ~1.62B tokens/mo (a modeled, pool-deduped aggregate, not a grant). But: Socket.dev blocked npm 3.8.5 in May 2026, 19 advisories May-Jul 2026 incl. unauthenticated RCE, ownership moved Oct 21, 2026 to cheaper-inference (a commercial reseller), and routing your prompts/keys through free tiers carries per-provider ToS risk. Standing exclusion in AGENTS.md.

repos.claim: 160+ skills for research agents (from the '7 repos' list).
repos.last_push: not captured (arXiv paper Sep 2, 2026; secondary sources Nov 2026 say now 177 skills / ~47k stars)
repos.reason: Real; the '160+' claim is true (163 in the paper, ~177 by Nov 2026). Science-research niche only - low utility outside that domain.

repos.claim: Diagrams for Claude Code workflows (from the '7 repos' list).
repos.reason: Real, popular, actively maintained (last commit Nov 22, 2026). Diagram skills for Claude Code workflows, as claimed.

repos.claim: Security skills for coding agents (from the '7 repos' list).
repos.last_push: not captured (~17,173 stars as of Jun 21, 2026)
repos.reason: Real community project (754-818 skills), but NOT affiliated with Anthropic despite the name - its own README says so. Includes offensive/dual-use techniques for authorized use only.

repos.claim: Orchestration patterns (from the '7 repos' list).
repos.reason: Real curated awesome-list of harness/orchestration patterns - a reading list, not a tool to install. Limited direct utility.

repos.claim: Context for your agents (from the '7 repos' list).
repos.reason: Real ByteDance/Volcengine project, actively maintained. AGPLv3 (relicensed from Apache-2.0 in Mar 2026) and heavy setup - license + effort limit its use for Ankit.

repos.claim: Persistent memory for coding agents (from the '7 repos' list).
repos.reason: Real repo per the dev.to mirror of the same 7-repo list (published Nov 16, 2026). Stars/last-push not captured in this audit; persistent-memory niche, moderate utility.

repos.claim: Open-source tool letting AI agents investigate how apps work without source code; 'blocked by code restrictions, OpenCode workaround lets REA deconstruct apps'; 'how to hack premium website features'.
repos.last_push: not captured (~109k stars Oct 2026; v6.7.0; 207 tools)
repos.reason: Real, very popular MCP server + skill. Install only from the official repo or npm 'rea-agents' (copycats exist). The 'blocked / OpenCode workaround' claim was not independently verified, and cloning commercial apps raises IP/ToS issues - use only on apps you own or have permission to inspect.

repos.claim: Free open-source AI sales agent / lead-gen tool: finds customers, does prospect research, writes personalized cold emails, tracks replies, manages pipeline 24/7; runs on your Claude Code subscription instead of an API bill; nothing sends without approval.
repos.reason: Real repo, but renamed Harvey -> Sellbird in Nov 2026 and relicensed MIT -> AGPL-3.0. NOT free to run: needs a paid Claude Pro/Max or ChatGPT plan plus a mailbox (~$7/mo). Drafts are held for approval by default, which matches the Reel; auto-send is out per standing rule (drafts only).

repos.claim: Free, open-source plugin with 42 skills for Claude; searches award space across 27 mileage programs, points vs cash price, cheapest transfer path, live transfer bonuses.
repos.reason: Real repo; 42 skills / 27 programs check out. Award search needs paid API keys (e.g. Seats.aero Pro), so it is not fully free to run. Useful only for points travel.

repos.how: Keyword-gated ('comment COUNCIL') + name ('Expert Council / Roast Room')
repos.claim: Claude slash command creating AI versions of real experts (Naval, Hormozi, Codie Sanchez) from their public content; advisors debate decisions; you can add an AI version of yourself.
repos.reason: Real repo; simulations built from public material of real experts, and the Reel itself states they are simulations, not the real people. Entertainment/ideation value only - treat advice as a remix of public content, not expert counsel.

repos.claim: 11 Claude Code skills that turn a vibe-coded app into a senior team's work (architect, tech lead, designer, copywriter, security + speed engineers); 'every role tested blind against the best free skill'.
repos.reason: Not a GitHub repo and not free: a paid $49 product (zip download) at deftskills.dev, presented as skills to be sent on comment. Blind-test scores are self-reported by the seller.

repos.claim: AI tool that tries to hack your application before real hackers do: multiple AI agents simulate real-world attacks, find vulnerabilities, report severity, attack details, fixes, step-by-step solutions.
repos.reason: Real official repo (a fork/mirror 'Itachi-Viper-Zero/strix' created Nov 16, 2026 looks like a copycat - use the official repo only). Needs Docker + an LLM API key, so not free to run. Test only apps you own or have permission to test.

repos.claim: One developer pointed a frontier model at the entire Adobe Creative Cloud suite and rebuilt it: Photoshop, Premiere, Lightroom - seven applications, open source, free, in Rust. 'Software is over.'
repos.last_push: not captured (PhotoCraft ~77,654 stars Nov 7, 2026; created Sep 30, 2026; early alpha)
repos.reason: Real org and project, broadly as reported, but the Reel overstates it: 5 apps in alpha, 12 in development - they are not replacements yet. Clean-room reimplementation claims carry trade-dress/patent risk, flagged by coverage.

repos.claim: Someone ran a 744B-parameter AI model (GLM-5.2) on a laptop without a graphics card; streams only 10GB of active parameters through RAM, rest from disk; runs fully offline, serves as an OpenAI endpoint with one code change.
repos.reason: Real repo and the architecture claim checks out (GLM-5.2 744B MoE, ~25GB RAM, ~10GB active), but it runs at 0.05-0.1 tokens/sec cold - not 'high-speed' - and needs a ~372GB model download. A fork 'sabalioglu/colibri-glm5.2' also exists.

repos.claim: 'Claude Code just released the Untangle Codebase skill' - cleans up messy projects by identifying duplicated logic, unnecessary wrappers, temporary workarounds.
repos.reason: Real community skill, but the Reel's attribution is false: it is by caldoai, NOT released by Anthropic/Claude Code. Small, niche cleanup utility.

repos.claim: Open-source job-hunting agent; no coding experience needed, setup in 5 minutes; author applied 69 times, 20 interviews, 1 contract (per dashboard/MEMORY context).
repos.last_push: not captured (~62k stars; No. 1 GitHub daily trending Oct 19, 2026; repo created Mar 2026; moved from MadsLorentzen/ai-job-search to ai-job-search-dev org)
repos.reason: Real, huge, and the 69/20/1 funnel is the author's own claim in the README - not independently verified (one audit found a 'Landed a job?' thread with no other hires reported). Real privacy gotcha: the fork the quick-start tells you to create is public, and /setup writes personal data into tracked files - two users already published personal data this way. Drafts only, never auto-sends. Already the basis of Ankit's CareerLaunch app.

repos.claim: YC CEO Garry Tan released a free skill that answers 'where to start automating' from your own meetings: install 'Idea Miner', connect your meeting note-taker, every morning it reads your last 2 days of meetings and suggests jobs to automate.
repos.last_push: not captured (~14,000 stars; released Apr 5, 2026; v0.16.4 era; 29-34 skills)
repos.reason: Real: GBrain is Garry Tan's open-source agent memory system (17,888 pages, 4,383 people, 723 companies in his own brain) and Idea Miner is a real skill in it. But it is not a standalone free skill - it needs the full GBrain setup plus a connected calendar and meeting note-taker (Granola/Circleback), and a hosted gbrain.io option exists. Counts are the author's own.

repos.claim: World's first 145-billion-parameter AI model that runs fully on a laptop, activating about 10 billion parameters at once, high-speed.
repos.last_push: released Nov 12, 2026 (v0.2.0 Nov 11, 2026; >10,000 stars at launch)
repos.license: Apache-2.0 (code; weights on Hugging Face Edge0/Edge0-145B-q3k, derived from Qwen3.8-Flash-Next)
repos.reason: Real launch (Nov 12, 2026): 145B total, ~10.12B active per token - the core claim checks out. But 'runs on a laptop' means a 48GB MacBook Pro or a 16GB+ VRAM NVIDIA GPU (CUDA 13), ~40-48GB download, and every speed/benchmark number is the vendor's own with no independent verification yet.

repos.repo: Jev AI / TypeSafe AI — NOT a GitHub repo
repos.claim: A former ChatGPT co-creator built an AI that doesn't write a single sentence; makes direct decisions (Choice, Score, Yes/No); claiming 200x faster speed and 400x lower cost.
repos.reason: Not a repo at all: Jev is a closed, hosted, paid API model from TypeSafe AI (founder Diogo Almeida; his own words are 'helped build the methods... that work ended up as the research behind ChatGPT' - 'co-creator' is press framing). 200x/400x are vendor claims; independent tests land narrower and Jev was not the most accurate in TypeSafe's own eval table. Cannot verify as a free/open tool.
